steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: Your uniform suits you.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: S-Supervisor! Zuo Le reporting.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: At ease. No need to be too uptight your first day on the job. Better that you maintain your youthful energy.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Understood, Supervisor!

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: Do you know where we are, Zuo Le?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: 'Upon the peaks was the beast cornered and killed.' This was the battlefield where we killed a Feranmut during the Great Hunt.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But...
Zuo Le pauses, unsure if he can continue, until he sees the patient gaze of the Supervisor.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: This was also where countless soldiers and civilians lost their lives... where living, breathing people faded into a graveyard of lines of cold numbers between the pages.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: You have realized something that many Candleholders older than you do not.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: 'Carry the fire that drives out the shadows of the Feranmut, and travel amongst the people to learn their troubles.'

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: It was the first Candleholder, holding the torch that discovered the existence of the Feranmuts, that made possible the war with the gods which secured Yan's future.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: Even today, the existence of Feranmuts is only known to a select few.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: Which makes it all the more important that the Candleholder's fire remains brightly lit where shadows fall.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I will do my utmost to protect the people.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: I am glad to see your resolve. But let me ask you again—what are the Feranmuts, in your eyes?

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: What are the proxies who live amongst us within the season, on whom we keep a constant watch?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The hearts of people are fickle; the hearts of beasts even more so. Perhaps some amongst Them have once aided Yan, be it out of a whim, or true sincerity.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But weighing the pros and cons, ultimately... They are different from us. They are... enemies.

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: Enemies, you say...

steps.name: Sui Regulator Supervisor
steps.text: ...Enemies.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Supervisor...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: That question should be mine to ask.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Where have you taken the token from the Garden of Grotesqueries after the Placation was completed?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Something was not right at the Sui Regulator, and scriptgeists were running amok in the Sky Mirror Pavilion. I wanted to wait for the situation to settle down before seeking your counsel...

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Then you can give it to me here.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I have heard that it was not the usual jade rule that was retrieved from the Garden of Grotesqueries this year. I will bring it back to the Sui Regulator for further investigation.
Acting on a subconscious instinct, Zuo Le finds himself taking a step back from his familiar superior.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: My, my. I did not think there would come a day when Candleholder Zuo defied his orders.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Cut the crap—you're Chun, head of the Sui Regulator?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: A Shanhaizhong member, in the Sky Mirror Pavilion. A highly ranked one, too, judging from your attire. Under normal circumstances, the Patrol Battalion would have faced severe penalties.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: And this is... Lady Ch'en?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You're Zuo Le's boss?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Though I am unworthy of this position, it is my duty.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: What are you doing here? Waiting for us to walk into a trap?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Unfortunately, it is not you that I am waiting for.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Hand over the token, Zuo Le, and you may leave with your friends. We can discuss your association with undesirable elements later.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: I thought you would tell him to take me in on the spot to make up for his transgressions.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: We are in the courts of Yan, not some bandit camp.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Fine enough for you to say.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Who was it who encouraged Jie to enter the Tomb of Sui, so that the more dangerous proxy for Yan would die in Wang's place, catapulting her own career in the process?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Yaan would be ashamed to have a descendant like you!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Mo Yi! The Supervisor is not like that!

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Really? Then why did she become the Supervisor so soon after Jie's death?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Only a thief sees thieves everywhere.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Keep your mouth shut, for you are not worthy to speak her name.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The imperial court of Yan does not pause or waver for any person or thing. All that it does is measured against the interests of Great Yan.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: The interests of Great Yan?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: It seems Lady Ch'en has something to say.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Very well. I will give you three minutes, in consideration of the risks that Zuo Le ran to retrieve this object from the Garden of Grotesqueries.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: There is someone I am waiting for anyway. Ask your questions, then leave the token and leave this place.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Waiting for someone?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Yes, waiting for someone.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Is it the proxy who holds the key?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Why do you say that?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Geists run rampant through Baizao, but Zuo Le is the only one who is trying to tackle the scriptgeists at the source, and on no orders at that.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: The L.G.D. was never so negligent, even when Wei Yenwu's oversight was at its laxest.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: The first thing you asked about when you saw Zuo Le was not the scriptgeists, but the token from the Garden of Grotesqueries... you seem to care nothing for your responsibilities.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The Sui Regulator is not the police.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Who in Baizao is more qualified than the Sui Regulator to deal with the scriptgeists?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Your goals are aligned with the Grand Commandant's... you want the writing knife.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: And if Mo Yi is telling the truth, no one in Baizao is closer to the writing knife than Jun.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You do the L.G.D. proud, superintendent.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Why are you assisting the Grand Commandant's plot? What do you plan to do with Wei Yenwu? Or have you already joined forces with him?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Plot?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You may have been an excellent officer of the law, Lady Ch'en, but it is not your place to intervene in matters of national interest.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I've been to places and seen things. There's no need for grandiose words.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: If your plot is indeed in the interest of the nation, you should feel no shame in saying it out loud.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Only those involved in political squabbles would keep bringing up 'national interest' when questioned, beating around the bush and deflecting the question.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You should be careful with your words, Lady Ch'en. The matters of state are complex and interconnected, and it is not unusual for officials to have differing views. Your words insult all who serve the state.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: For a thousand years, the Sui Regulator has had one mission, and one alone—to do what is best for Yan in matters pertaining to Feranmuts. Nothing else matters to us.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Even if the Grand Commandant's actions are indeed drastic, extraordinary times call for extraordinary measures. The use of the writing knife does not constitute treason.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Then what is he planning—

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: At this point, I doubt this damned old Elf is gonna talk, so I'll do the talking for her.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Just as I suspected—the Grand Commandant wants to rewrite history with the writing knife and completely eliminate the bestial Sui. The price is the True Lung's life.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But why... what does the True Lung's life have to do with destroying a Feranmut?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: We were just talking about it, before we were interrupted... a thousand years ago, the grandmaster discovered a piece of Originium that he presented to the True Lung as a weapon that can end the Great Hunt.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Realizing its importance, the True Lung had his Fangshi perform a ritual that linked it to True Lung's bloodline.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Henceforth, the power of the Originium may only be harnessed by the reigning True Lung.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: That True Lung had a bit of a conscience, at least, and he set a condition in the ritual, probably to prevent his descendants from abusing it—

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: The full power of the Originium can only be unleashed by sacrificing the life of the True Lung. Hence it was given the name Bu Fan—'No Rebellion'.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: But does the True Lung's life to be sacrificed really have to be the emperor's? Why did the Grand Commandant go to such painstaking lengths to obtain this writing knife, if his goal was merely a coup?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You mean... the Grand Commandant wants to use the writing knife to change the record of who the current True Lung is?!

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: 'The Grand Preceptor incited the prince to regicide.'

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: What is the truth of what happened that night? Who sent the Yulin Guard away? Who actually entered the emperor's chambers? These things are not specified in the records...

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Therefore, the records of what happened that night can still be rewritten using the writing knife.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: If the history books and Bu Fan recognize Lord Wei as the reigning True Lung, then the life of the True Lung obviously refers to Lord Wei's life.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I had thought that you were young, and that though you may have strayed from the righteous path, you should be given the chance to right your wrongs.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Regrettably, it seems I cannot allow you to live.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Not putting on a show of honesty and uprightness anymore, are we?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Supervisor!

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Hand over the token, Zuo Le! Whatever happens after that is none of your concern!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: If what Mo Yi says is true... then I voice my dissent to your methods, Supervisor.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I cannot comply.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I don't want to damage the Sky Mirror Pavilion... don't make me do this.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You're talking to the wrong person. I have the token—
Ch'en's vision is obstructed by several maple leaves. The lamplight sways slightly.
Ch'en steps back and prepares to engage, only for Mo Yi to step forward and block Chun's attack.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: So the Supervisor of the Sui Regulator is not above sneak attacks... like a thief.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: One can be subtle and reserved with words, but action must be decisive and without hesitation. It is as true in weiqi as it is with all things in life.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Supervisor...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I have read about the writing knife in the past. In Jie's hands, it can indeed alter history and greatly influence events.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But we are not proxies. Our tampered historical records will never endure for long!

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: An instant is all it takes to activate Bu Fan.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Besides...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: After this, there will no longer be a disgraced deposed crown prince in Yan, only a pure True Lung whose legitimacy is beyond question—is that right?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: That is not the Sui Regulator's concern.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Since her death, Great Yan's history is already in tatters. One more change will hardly make a difference—

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: How can you be so sure that we cannot record history truthfully?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien... Magistrate of Water for the Sky Mirror Pavilion.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I wanted to ask you as well, Supervisor...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: For many years, you assisted Jie in compiling history in her office... why is it that you have now turned to tampering with history?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The records of Yan are classified into four parts: Classics, History, Philosophy, and Literature.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The divisions of History and Philosophy may seem distinct, but even the masterwork of the one venerated as the Saint of History was, merely the personal treatise within Philosophy.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Those who follow, modeling their brushes after his style, produce what is ultimately but the statement of a single house, and the House of Yan.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Those writings are no more than comments after the fact. The truth has long faded into the cracks of time.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: How could you say that?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: You must have read the Saint of History's notes. Despite imprisonment and torture, he always wrote the facts as they were and exposed injustice.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: You must have read the history tomes of the Sky Mirror Pavilion, written by thousands of sages who poured their hearts and souls into them, striving to set the record straight, to weigh every word in judgment of right and wrong.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: You must have heard of unofficial historians—meticulously investigating and analyzing their sources, coveting not the court's wealth and rank, but striving only to uphold justice for the common people.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I saw with my own eyes the elders of my family dying on white fields of snow because they wanted to write down the truth... nay, because they were honest to themselves!

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: These people, who wrote history with their own flesh and blood, who willingly became the flame to illuminate the truth even for a moment—

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Who are they to you, Supervisor?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: They are the writers.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: True and false, right and wrong, these things always depend on the stance of the writer, rather than on what is actually right.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You ought to know—even with the revisions of countless esteemed scholars, the histories we read are still rife with embellishment, omissions and lies.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The ironic thing is... we could not even call such things 'evil'.
The curled leaves make a sharp sound against each other, questioningly, lamentingly.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Stand back, Ch'en Chao-ch'ien. You are neither Candleholder, nor Shanhaizhong, nor the niece of a deposed crown prince. This is not your fight.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Did the Imperial Historical Cabinet truly take up responsibility for writing history after her passing? Did the Sky Mirror Pavilion truly fulfill its duty of righting the wrongs?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You are the descendant of historians. If you take up their mantle, can you truly guarantee that every word will be true for all eternity?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: No. You dare not shoulder this responsibility.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I know about you.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You wanted to change the Sky Mirror Pavilion's culture of obsession with the analysis of ancient history while neglecting recent history. That's why you took up a minor position at the Sky Mirror Pavilion, hoping to lead by example by studying your family's history.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Decades, centuries, millennia. How could you claim to speak for history, when you have not borne witness to time on the scale that she knew?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Stand back.
The maple leaves sharpen.
This time, no one saw what Chun did. All she did was wave her sleeve; the next instant, Ch'en Chao-ch'ien was lying unconscious on the floor.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Chao-ch'ien?!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Supervisor—

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: She's just unconscious. She'll wake up in a couple of hours. There is no need for her to sink any deeper into this mire. She's but an unfortunate ordinary woman. She shouldn't have to be like you... or like me.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I hear Elves live a long time.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: We do.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You don't believe in history or in lasting justice in people's hearts... because the one who had walked side-by-side with you on the long road of time died because of you?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: This question is not yours to ask, Ch'en Hui-chieh.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: As an Elf, you don't know where you came from, whether there are any of your kind left, or whether there'll ever be a home for you—

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: My past, present and future belong to Yan.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: And that involves tossing your fellows into the abyss?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Having her die in Wang's place was the appropriate decision under the circumstances! This is beyond all doubt!

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Compiling history, recording the passage of time... have you any idea of the power of these 'years', the power of time?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: 'The beast walks with the generous earth.' She had gone one step further. Her power was rooted in words, and lived in history. As long as the records of Yan continued, her power would continue to grow without end.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: If left unchecked, what sort of monster would be created in the end? It would be something even more powerful, even more terrible than Sui itself!

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: She was my mentor, my confidant, my friend. But I could not endanger Great Yan with my own selfish interests.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I've seen people like you... people who abandoned their friends, but long to see them again in dreams, in order to beg for forgiveness.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Head of the Sui Regulator, what would you do if there was a way to see her again?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I warn you, do not play games with the lives of millions for the fantasies of a madman!

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Wang did not go into the Tomb of Sui for the sole purpose of eliminating Sui.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The object that he had you retrieve from the Garden of Grotesqueries surely has something to do with his deranged plans to bring the dead back to life.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: I'm surprised... I thought you got along well with her when you were her Candleholder.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Isn't there a part of you, somewhere, that wants his plan to succeed?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: He already failed a hundred and twenty years ago. He will fail again. Allowing him to continue on his reckless path will only lead to more disaster.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: How can I trust a madman who treats heaven and earth as his weiqi board, and all lives and souls as his pieces? How can I trust a sinner who caused the death of his sister?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: How can I trust the obsession of a Feranmut?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Because, like you, he walked this land, lived in the seasons, and vowed to become 'human', to become part of this land and those who live upon it.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: 'Human'?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Humans are humans because they live and die. This is why they shine, as the candle's fleeting glow.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: She has lived, and she has died. Wang seeks to disturb the slumber of the dead, in defiance of the laws of Heaven.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Even if his delusions somehow came true, how can you be sure that it is the departed herself who has returned and not a geist, a hollow puppet that only carries her image?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You just don't want to believe.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Things seldom go the way people want them to.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: The outcome may not be exactly what we want. But to be shackled by regret and not even have the courage to take a single step...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...That is nothing but cowardice.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: You have a way with words, Ch'en Hui-chieh. But I don't see how you intend to carry out the justice you speak of.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The token and the key. I am only here for them.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Continue to play games with words, and I will crush you before dealing with them.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Let's see who's crushing who.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: What about you, Zuo Le?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I apologize, but I must cause offense.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Hah. So be it.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Those who stay near ink get stained. You have made some good friends, Candleholder Zuo.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Do your worst.
